elevenlabs.source: GET /v1/models model_rates.character_cost_multiplier: a character costs that many credits at list price; a library voice's rate (GET /v1/voices/{id} sharing.rate) multiplies it
elevenlabs.note: Measured on a Starter plan, 13 October 2026: the request kind (a line or a dialogue), stability and the other voice settings, language_code, previous_text and next_text (not billed), the output format, the endpoint with or without timestamps and a premade or library voice at rate 1 do not change the share billed, so no setting is a price setting.

periods.source: Measured on 28 October 2026 (23:10 UTC): the character-cost header of POST /v1/sound-generation said 10 credits a second of sound, whether its length was set or chosen by the service. ElevenLabs' documentation, read the same day, said 40 credits a second with the length set: what the account is billed is the measure kept. Sound effects are not in GET /v1/history, so `pnpm run costs:record` does not see them: they are recorded by hand.

discount.source: The launch discount, announced as 72 % « until October 12 »: $0.08 → $0.022 per 1,000 characters (https://www.eesel.ai/blog/eleven-v4-pricing, https://pricingsaas.com/companies/elevenlabs/diffs/2026D273); the account's history shows it until 2026-10-13T01:09:33Z and the full price from 07:27:07Z, so it ended at midnight Pacific time. GET /v1/models cost_discount_multiplier said 1 once it had ended; whether it said the discount while it ran is not known.

periods.source: Eleven v4 launched on 28 September 2026 (the hour is not known); list price as GET /v1/models says it.

discount.source: The launch discount on v4 and v4 Turbo: $0.04 → $0.011 per 1,000 characters for Turbo (https://www.eesel.ai/blog/eleven-v4-pricing); its end as Eleven v4's, not measured on Turbo.

periods.source: Eleven v4 Turbo launched with Eleven v4 on 28 September 2026.
